chunks: So he came from the chamber to his people, and suggested to them (by signs) to sing the praises of the Lord morning and evening.

key_terms.الْمِحْرَابِ: The chamber or prayer niche, often referring to a place of worship or seclusion.
key_terms.فَأَوْحَى: He inspired or conveyed divine message/revelation.

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Zakariyya convey to his people when he came out of the mihrab?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah Maryah, Prophet Zakariyya (AS) emerges from his mihrab to deliver a concise divine message, emphasizing the importance of consistent dhikr (remembrance) as a spiritual anchor. Shia scholars highlight this as a model of prophetic leadership, where the leader transitions from private devotion to public exhortation, urging the community to maintain spiritual vigilance through morning and evening glorification. This continuous rhythm of worship reflects the balance between worldly duties and spiritual connection, a key theme in Shia ethical teachings.
